title: Games with AI Assets that were favorably received?
author: greatblueplanet
selftext:
We all know games that were review bombed by people who hate AI. 

A lot of them are slop, though.

Have there been well-made games that use AI that were well-received?

comments.author: lordaloa
comments.body:
As I stated before.  It does not matter to general consumers wheter you used AI. There is some zealots but generally, generic games don’t care.

HOWEVER what they DO care about in general is the quality of the product. If you try to 1 shot a game through AI and people say it feels like an AI cash grab then your game prolly is.

You still need to put in the touch that makes your game stand out, feel and play very good and be oleasing to the eye.

The market has become even more saturated then ever so it will take even more skill (as designer developer etc) to work and create a product people want to notice.

Yes use AI id you don’t use AI you could be handicapping yourself but BE THE DEVELOPER do not let AI guide your vision. Be the owner of your own product.

replies.author: SnuffleBag
replies.body:
This is not what market research seems to says - in fact there seems to be a growing amount of dislike towards generative AI in games the past two years. It's nowhere near the witchhunt factors you see on reddit, but it's also not a factor to just completely ignore.

There's of course a gazillion different reports and articles all coming to their own conclusion, but to provide at least one source with my claims, here's a fairly recent one with some additional links inside: [https://www.athena-productions.com/read/state-of-ai-2026-246](https://www.athena-productions.com/read/state-of-ai-2026-246)

replies.author: bieker
replies.body:
I think the problem right now is that it’s moving to too fast. That article relies allot on data from the Game Oracle analysis from December 2025 which analyzed data from games disclosing AI usage during the first three quarters of 2025.  At the time those games were in development AI was much less powerful and workflows were less well developed. And that study admits that the data shows that the effect of AI disclosure is less than the noise floor of the data. 

I would love to see a detailed analysis like that of more recent data.

replies.author: SnuffleBag
replies.body:
I completely agree that it's a fast moving part of the industry and data gets old really really fast. 

That being said, I still want to see a bit more than some guy's claim on what is probably reddit's most pro-AI forum saying "*As I stated before. It does not matter*". It definitely does matter. It's hard to know exactly how much it matters this month, but I feel pretty confident saying that sentiment has not gone from "*63% of gamer attitudes were overall very negative about generative AI*" to "*nobody cares*" in less than a year.

replies.author: Viktorkin
replies.body:
I wonder how much of that reporting is related to AI games being easier to release. I would expect Ai games to get less sales, less reviews, and lower scores on average because there are a TON of them where the dev didn't do anything to make the game good. That would bring averages down, but doesnt really tell us about the sentiment itself. 

I am nervous about the vocally anti Ai crowd though. A developer friend and I have spent years working on a tcg. In my opinion its fun, has cool features that we designed and built, and pretty varied gameplay from match to match.

Unfortunately neither of us are artists. There's 350ish cards in the game. The cost to illustrate those would be 50k + that we just dont have, so we're using genAI images, at least for now. Im not stoked about it, and I've saved a dozen or so artists who id love to pay, but $500 per card for two guys working on a side project just isn't feasible. I worry that just buries the game and allows people to ignore hundreds of hours of actual dev and design work that's gone into it.

Sorry for rambling a bit lol!

replies.author: SnuffleBag
replies.body:
That's definitely a factor, and there's a fairly lengthy discussion about this in the linked Game Oracle article trying to work out how/when/why/who it affects to which degree.

I'm not really in a position to give advice about your situation. But if it was me, I would be completely honest in the disclaimer, but just try to not engage with the online communities that I already know to have preconveiced opinions - because I just wouldn't need that headache, and it's a discussion that can't be won.

replies.author: Viktorkin
replies.body: Yeah that's the plan. I have no interest in trying to "dupe" anyone. Hoping the gameplay speaks for itself!

replies.author: bieker
replies.body: I would not spend too much time thinking about it. 70% of games releasing on Steam now include AI disclosures including most of the big studios. And the majority of those disclosures mention in game art.

replies.author: Blueberry_Gecko
replies.body: But I'm a pretty general consumer and it does matter to me..? The thing is, even if you oneshot an excellent game with Claude, why would I care about something that *you* didn't care about? In this fictional scenario, I could instead play any of a million other games that are also good and were also oneshot by Claude *and* had someone that cared about them and are therefore strictly better games on average.

comments.author: wirthmore
comments.body:
EA College Football 

[https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/ea-ceo-says-studio-needed-genai-for-ea-college-football-25-development](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/ea-ceo-says-studio-needed-genai-for-ea-college-football-25-development)

>Previous sports games required 500-1,000 star heads, but *College 25* had 11,000.  
  
Use cases like College Football 25’s seem to justify the use of genAI, as they make large-scale projects viable and don’t seem to replace human workers. Questions still remain on what, if any, datasets the tech was trained on.

It was trained on their library of 11,000 photos of college football athletes who consented and were paid to have their likenesses used in the game. The history: [https://www.hbsslaw.com/cases/ncaa-video-games](https://www.hbsslaw.com/cases/ncaa-video-games)

replies.author: SnuffleBag
replies.body:
I'm not gonna blow the whistle, but IMHO it's an unnecessary liability to under-report the actual involvement of gen-AI when you have a commercially successful game on your hands.



>a LOT is hand fixed after

Valve's rules don't care about this, you can't wash the AI of an asset.

Good luck with your game in either case.

replies.author: lyeeedar
replies.body: I'm not sure why you think it's a liability? Valves rules are only that you have to disclose IF AI is used. But they have no rules on how you phrase it or what you say. In fact, they have no guidance at all. I'll be the first to update it to be compliant if they change, but for now it's opinion only on what's the right way to do it.
